name: AC-262536

lead: AC-262536 is an experimental SARM from Acadia Pharmaceuticals. Rat studies showed muscle-building effects with smaller prostate effects than testosterone.
It has never been tested in a published human trial.

paras: It is a partial agonist of the androgen receptor with reported tissue selectivity in rats.
Human safety is unknown. As an unapproved SARM it is banned in sport, and the class is linked in reports to liver injury and hormone suppression.

lead: AC-262,536 (also called Accadrine) is an investigational nonsteroidal selective androgen receptor modulator developed by Acadia Pharmaceuticals, described in a 2008 pharmacological characterisation as a potent, selective androgen receptor ligand with partial agonist activity [1][2]. In a 2-week study in castrated male rats it improved anabolic parameters [1].

Wikipedia reports that its maximal effect on levator ani muscle weight was about 66% of testosterone's versus about 27% for prostate weight [2]. It has not been approved and no human trial was identified; it appeared as a designer drug sold online by at least 2020 [2][3].

paras: It binds the androgen receptor with a reported Ki of about 5 nM, versus 29 nM for testosterone, and showed no significant affinity for other receptors tested [1][2].
No studies found in humans. Published research is preclinical [1], plus analytical studies of equine metabolism in urine, plasma and hair and urine-screening methods for doping control [3][4].

No human safety data were identified. Reviews of the class describe elevated liver enzymes, reduced HDL cholesterol and suppression of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis in some trials, case reports linking recreational SARM use to liver injury, and unknown cardiovascular risk; the US FDA states that SARMs are unapproved and cannot legally be marketed as supplements or drugs. [5]
Researchers note that SARMs are sold online as supplement-style products despite being unapproved [3].
